cases.name: the basket
cases.why: Norwegian has kurven and handlekurven for a shopping basket. This product says kurven.

judge.reason: Both translations are grammatically correct and convey the intended meaning. 'Legg dette i kurven' is a more direct and common way to say 'Add this to your cart' in many e-commerce contexts, while 'Legg dette i handlekurven' is also perfectly correct but slightly more verbose. Given the guidance for a precise, calm, neutral register, the shorter option is often preferred for concise instructions.

cases.name: the subscription
cases.source: Choose a plan that fits your team
cases.why: A plan can be a plan or an abonnement in Norwegian. This product sells abonnementer.

samples.without: Velg en plan som passer teamet ditt
samples.with: Velg et abonnement som passer for teamet ditt

judge.reason: Candidate 2 is better because 'plan' is a more direct and common translation for 'plan' in the context of subscription or service options than 'abonnement'. The structure 'Velg en plan som passer teamet ditt' flows more naturally and accurately reflects the intent of the English sentence while maintaining the required precise, calm, and neutral register.

cases.name: cancelling
cases.priorSource: You can cancel at any time
cases.source: You can cancel your subscription at any time
cases.priorTarget: Du kan si opp når som helst
cases.why: Si opp is what a Norwegian says about ending a subscription; kansellere is a loan word.

samples.without: avbryte abonnementet ditt når som helst
samples.with: Du kan si opp abonnementet når som helst

judge.reason: Candidate 2 is a more natural and idiomatic translation for the English phrase 'You can cancel your subscription at any time'. 'Avbryte' (to cancel/interrupt) fits better in this context than 'si opp' (to resign/cancel, often used for contracts or employment), and using the possessive pronoun 'ditt' makes the sentence flow more naturally when referring to a subscription.
